chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى صَفْوَانُ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ:

translations.en: And Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ جَارِيَةٍ لَمْ تَحِضْ خَرَجَتْ مَعَ زَوْجِهَا وَ أَهْلِهَا فَحَاضَتْ فَاسْتَحْيَتْ أَنْ تُعْلِمَ أَهْلَهَا وَ زَوْجَهَا حَتَّى قَضَتِ الْمَنَاسِكَ وَ هِيَ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ وَ وَاقَعَهَا زَوْجُهَا وَ رَجَعَتْ إِلَى الْكُوفَةِ فَقَالَتْ لِأَهْلِهَا قَدْ كَانَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ كَذَا وَ كَذَا

translations.en: I asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام about a young woman who had not menstruated before. She went out with her husband and her family, then she menstruated, but was too shy to inform her family and her husband, until she completed the rites while in that state. Her husband had intercourse with her, and she returned to al-Kufah. Then she said to her family: such-and-such had happened.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ «عَلَيْهَا سَوْقُ بَدَنَةٍ وَ الْحَجُّ مِنْ قَابِلٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى زَوْجِهَا شَيْءٌ.

translations.en: So he عليه السلام said: "She must drive a camel as an offering, and the hajj is to be performed again the following year, and there is nothing upon her husband."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who menstruated during hajj, concealed it out of shyness, completed the rites in that state, and later had intercourse with her husband. The Imam عليه السلام rules that she must offer a camel and repeat the hajj the following year, while no penalty falls upon the husband because he was unaware.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman menstruates during hajj, hides it, completes the rites, and her husband has intercourse with her?

key_terms.بَدَنَةٍ: a camel offered as sacrificial expiation
key_terms.الْحَجُّ مِنْ قَابِلٍ: repeating the hajj in the following year
